newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-STEADY RAIN CONTINUES TO PLAGUE WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-STEADY RAIN CONTINUES TO PLAGUE WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Steady rain was still falling on Wimbledon on Thursday, more than two hours after the day's scheduled start, and the prospects of play getting underway looked bleak.
Rain prevented all but two matches being completed on Wednesday and organisers had hoped to start early on Thursday in a bid to eat into the backlog.

But at 1.30 p.m. local time (1230 GMT) the Centre Court at the All England Club presented a forlorn picture with just a few hardy fans huddled under umbrellas watching the rain fall on the court cover.
World number one Martina Hingis had been due to open the day's action on Centre Court against Olga Barabanshchikova of Belarus at 1100 GMT in a second-round match.
Matches on the outside courts had been due to start an hour earlier.
Weather forecasters offered little comfort, saying the rain was expected to continue for most of the day and into Friday.

But organisers refused to despair, saying the situation was better than in 1991 when only 54 matches were completed in the first four days and officials decided to play on the middle Sunday, traditionally a rest day, for the first time in Wimbledon history.
This year, 93 matches have been played so far.
"They will still be well ahead if we get nothing today," a spokesman for tournament referee Alan Mills said.

Asked about the prospect of playing on Sunday again, the spokesman said: "They are not keen on the idea and there is no guarantee the weather will be great anyway. The forecast is no better for Sunday."
All the doubles matches scheduled for Thursday were postponed in the early afternoon as the rain continued. The doubles competitions have yet to start.
